chunks: Our father narrated, may God be pleased with him, saying: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab, from al-Hakam ibn Maskin al-Thaqafi, from Salih ibn Aqbah, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon him) who said: When Abu Bakr died and Umar took the caliphate, Umar returned to the mosque and sat down. A man entered and said to him: 'O Commander of the Faithful! I am a Jew and their scholar. I intend to ask you about some matters; if you answer me, I will embrace Islam.' He said: 'What are they?' He said: 'Three, three, and one. If you wish, I will ask you, and if there is someone among the people more knowledgeable than you, guide me to him.' He said: 'Go to that young man,' meaning Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him). So the man went to Ali (peace be upon him) and asked him. Ali said to him: 'Why did you say three, three, and one, and not seven?' He said: 'Because I would be ignorant if you could not answer the first three, I would be content.' He said: 'If I answer you, will you accept Islam?' He said: 'Yes.' He said: 'Ask.' He said: 'I ask you about the first rock placed on the face of the Earth, the first spring that gushed forth, and the first tree that sprouted?'

He said: 'O Jew! You say that the first rock placed on the face of the Earth was the one in Bayt al-Maqdis (Jerusalem), but you lie. It was the rock with which Adam descended from Paradise.' He said: 'You are truthful, by God, it is in the handwriting of Harun and dictated by Musa.' He said: 'And you say that the first spring to gush on the face of the Earth was the one in Bayt al-Maqdis, but you lie. It is the Spring of Life in which Yusha ibn Nun washed the fish, and it is the spring from which al-Khadr drank, and no one drinks from it except that he becomes alive (immortal).' He said: 'You are truthful, by God, it is in the handwriting of Harun and dictated by Musa.' He said: 'And you say that the first tree to sprout on the face of the Earth was the olive tree, but you lie. It was the Ajwa date with which Adam (peace be upon him) descended from Paradise with him.' He said: 'You are truthful, by God, it is in the handwriting of Harun and dictated by Musa.'

He said: 'And the other three: How many guiding Imams are there for this Ummah, such that those who abandon them do not harm them?' He said: 'Twelve Imams.' He said: 'You are truthful, by God, it is in the handwriting of Harun and dictated by Musa.' He said: 'Then where does your Prophet dwell in Paradise?' He said: 'In its highest degree and most noble place, in the Garden of Eden.' He said: 'You are truthful, by God, it is in the handwriting of Harun and dictated by Musa.' Then he said: 'And who will succeed him in his residence?' He said: 'Twelve Imams.' He said: 'You are truthful, by God, it is in the handwriting of Harun and dictated by Musa.' Then he asked the seventh question and accepted Islam: 'How long will his successor live after him?' He said: 'Thirty years.' He said: 'Then what? Does he die or is he killed?' He said: 'He is killed; he is struck on his horn (temple) and his beard is dyed (with blood).' He said: 'You are truthful, by God, it is in the handwriting of Harun and dictated by Musa.' And I have recorded this hadith from various chains in the book Al-Awal.

key_terms.الْأَوَائِلُ: Al-Awal, a book of early traditions

ai.seo_question: What were the seven questions asked by the Jewish scholar to Ali ibn Abi Talib that led to his conversion?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Khisal highlights the concept of 'Ilm al-Ghaib' (knowledge of the unseen) possessed by the Imams, validated through their ability to cite specific details from the Torah ('khat Harun wa imla Musa'). It structurally mirrors the twelve tribes of Israel with the twelve Imams, reinforcing the Shia doctrine of divine appointment (Nass) and the continuity of spiritual authority after the Prophet.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 12-41 (The compiler of the book narrated) that his father - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Sa’ed ibn Abdullah quoted Muhammad ibn al-Hussein ibn Abil Khat’tab, on the authority of Al-Hikam ibn Meskin al-Saqafy, on the authority of Salih ibn Aqabah, on the authority of Ja’far ibn Muhammad as-Sadiq (MGB), When Abu Bakr died and Umar took over the Caliphate, Umar went to the mosque and sat down. A man entered the mosque and said, ‘O commander of the faithful (referring to Umar)! I am one of the Jews. I am their great scholar. I wish to ask you about some problems. I will embrace Islam if you can convince me.’ Umar said, ‘What are they?’ He said, ‘Three, three and one. I will ask you if you please or guide me to ask anyone else who is more knowledgeable if you wish.’ Umar said, ‘Go and ask that young fellow who is Ali ibn Abi Talib (MGB).’ The Jew went to Ali (MGB) and asked him questions. Ali (MGB) said, ‘Why did you say three, three and one but did not say seven?’ The Jew said, ‘That would have been due to my ignorance! If you could not answer the first three questions, there would be no need to ask the rest.’ Ali (MGB) said, ‘Will you accept Islam if I give you the correct answers?’ The Jew said, ‘Yes, I will.’ Then Ali (MGB) said, ‘Go ahead and ask.’ The Jew asked, ‘Which were the first rock placed on the Earth, the first spring which gushed out of the Earth and the first tree which grew on the Earth?’

Ali (MGB) replied, ‘O Jew! You say that the first rock placed on the Earth was the one in Bayt ul- Muqadas (Holy Shrine in Jerusalem), but you lie. It was the rock which Adam brought down to the Earth from Heaven. You say that the first spring which gushed out of the Earth was one in Bayt ul-Muqadas (Holy Shrine in Jerusalem) but you lie. That spring was the spring of youth in which Yushu ibn Noon washed the fish and the same one from which Khizr drank. Whoever drinks from it will become eternal.’ The Jew said, ‘You are right. This has been recorded in Aaron’s handwriting on the authority of Moses.’ Then Ali (MGB) continued, ‘You say that the first tree which grew on the Earth was an olive tree but you lie. It was the Al-Ajwatdate which Adam brought down to the Earth from Heaven.’ The Jew said, ‘You are right. This has been recorded in Aaron’s handwriting on the authority of Moses.’

Then the Jew asked, ‘Where in Paradise does your Prophet sit?’ Ali (MGB) said, ‘In the noblest and highest place in the Adan Gardens.’ The Jew said, ‘You are right. This has been recorded in Aaron’s handwriting on the authority of Moses.’ Then the Jew asked, ‘Who will accompany him in his place of residence?’ Ali (MGB) replied, ‘The twelve Divine Leaders.’ The Jew said, ‘You are right. This has been recorded in Aaron’s handwriting on the authority of Moses.’ Then the Jew asked the seventh question and accepted Islam. He asked, ‘For how many years will his Trustee live after him?’ Ali (MGB) said, ‘Thirty years.’ He asked, ‘Will he die or will he get killed?’ Ali (MGB) replied, ‘He will be killed with such a blow on the head that his beard will become red with his blood.’ The Jew said, ‘You are right. This has been recorded in Aaron’s handwriting on the authority of Moses.’”I have recorded this book from its various chains of narrators in Awael.
